theme: The commandments as wisdom, sweeter than honey
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 119:97-144. Today’s section includes one of the most famous verses in the psalm, verse 105. Read it as a prayer from someone who loves God’s word and finds it a guide in the dark.
settingTheScene: The third section of Psalm 119 begins with a cry of love: “Oh how I love your law!” It speaks of wisdom, guidance, and zeal. The psalmist is surrounded by wicked people who do not keep God’s word, and he is grieved by their disobedience. Yet he finds in Scripture light, wisdom, and sweetness, and he holds to it with passion.
observation: “Oh how I love your law! It is my meditation all the day” (v. 97).
“Your commandment makes me wiser than my enemies, for it is ever with me” (v. 98).
“I have more understanding than all my teachers, for your testimonies are my meditation” (v. 99).
“How sweet are your words to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth!” (v. 103).
“Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path” (v. 105).
“I have sworn an oath and confirmed it, to keep your righteous rules” (v. 106).
“The unfolding of your words gives light; it imparts understanding to the simple” (v. 130).
“My eyes shed streams of tears, because people do not keep your law” (v. 136).
interpretation:
This section opens with an outpouring of love. The psalmist says it is his meditation all day long. It is not a duty that he squeezes in. It is the way he thinks. And the result is wisdom. He is wiser than his enemies, has more insight than his teachers, and understands more than the elders. These are not boasts about his intellect. He attributes it all to the word. The person who meditates on Scripture gains a wisdom that cleverness cannot give.

Verse 103 is one of the best descriptions of what it is to love the word: “How sweet are your words to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth.” It is a picture of delight. God’s word is not bitter medicine. It is food that we enjoy. In Ezekiel 3:3, the prophet eats a scroll and says it is as sweet as honey. In Revelation 10:9-10, John eats a scroll that is sweet in the mouth and bitter in the stomach. The word is sweet, but it can also be bitter, because it brings both joy and conviction.

Verse 105 is the best known: “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.” It is a modest image. A lamp in the ancient world did not light a whole road. It showed the next few steps. This is how God usually guides us. We do not get a floodlight on the whole future. We get enough to take the next step. The word is for walking, not just for knowing.

Verse 130 says that the unfolding of God’s words gives light to the simple. The word is not only for the educated. The humble and the simple can understand what is essential. God is not hiding his truth from them.

The last verses show the other side: the psalmist weeps because others do not keep the law. Love for God’s word includes grief for those who reject it. A heart that is in tune with God will be broken by what breaks his.
connection: Jesus is the light of the world (John 8:12), and he said, “Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness.” John says that the Word is the light that shines in the darkness (John 1:1-5). Paul says that the word of Christ should dwell in you richly (Colossians 3:16). Peter calls us to long for “the pure spiritual milk” of the word, “that by it you may grow up into salvation” (1 Peter 2:2). Jesus wept over Jerusalem (Luke 19:41).
application:
Memorize verse 105. Say it before you go out this week.

Ask what the “next step” is that the lamp is showing you now.

Let your heart be moved for those who do not know God’s word. Pray for someone by name.
prayerPrompts: Tell God what you love about his word, and what you find hard about it.
Ask him for understanding as you meditate on it today.
Ask him to give you a heart for those who do not know him.
